transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. Um, I guess what made me come in today is... I just keep feeling like I've ruined things for everybody. 

It's been really bothering me. I feel like I'm a total fake in my plumbing apprenticeship, and that I'm just letting my family and the younger apprentices down. And it's over stuff that... well, I know other people would probably just fix the mistake and move on from it, but I just can't seem to do that. I just feel like a massive letdown all the time lately.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Um, I'd say it's been about nine months. This whole stretch of feeling down has just been with me for a while now. I guess it really just became a lot harder to hide once my school and the apprenticeship work started slipping.
During these past nine months, have there been any periods of a few weeks or longer where you felt completely like your normal, happy self?
Um, no, not really. I don't think there's been any time like that. It's just been this same heavy feeling the whole time... I haven't really had a break where I felt like my normal self at all.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or your weight since this feeling started nine months ago?

Um, no, not really. I mean, my appetite seems pretty much the same as it always has been. I haven't noticed any weight gain or weight loss or anything like that. It's just the mood stuff that's been the problem.
How has your sleep been during these past nine months?

Um, it's been kind of all over the place, honestly. For a while there, I was getting by on maybe three or four hours a night, and I'd still show up completely wired for the job and my classes. But now... it's just really frustrating. I either can't fall asleep at all, or I wake up way before my alarm and just feel like I never even rested.
During that time when you were sleeping only three or four hours and felt 'wired,' did you also feel unusually energetic, talkative, or like your thoughts were racing?

Yeah, I definitely felt unusually energetic. It was like I had this... this nonstop charge in my body. I would work a full day on the pipes, and then I'd still go to my evening classes. And even after all that, instead of just sitting down to relax, I'd go home and reorganize all my tools, clean my entire apartment, and just start drawing up new systems. I just didn't really want to stop and sit.
During that time when you were feeling wired and energetic, did that period ever cause you to have serious problems at work, get into trouble, or require you to be hospitalized?

Um, no, nothing like that. I didn't get into any trouble, and I definitely wasn't in the hospital or anything. If anything, I was getting a ton done at work, so my boss didn't have any complaints. It didn't cause any serious problems, I just... I just had a lot of energy.
Looking back further than the last nine months, have you ever experienced any other periods in your life where you felt that same 'wired,' high-energy way for several days or longer?

Um, no, I don't think so. I mean, I've had times where I felt good or energetic, but nothing like that specific period where I was only sleeping a few hours and going nonstop. That was pretty unique. So, no, I haven't really had any other times like that before.
Aside from feeling like a letdown, have you noticed any other changes, such as having trouble concentrating on your work or feeling like life isn't worth living?

Well, my concentration has been okay, I guess, but... I do have these moments. I don't have some plan to hurt myself or anything like that. But sometimes, like when I'm driving home after class, or just lying awake at night, I get these thoughts. I just start thinking that it would be easier if I just didn't wake up tomorrow. It's just... it just crosses my mind.
During that time when you felt wired and energetic, did you find that you were more talkative than usual, felt like your thoughts were racing, or felt more important or capable than you usually do?

Well, I didn't really feel more important or anything, and my thoughts weren't exactly racing. But I definitely talked a lot more. Like, in class or when I was working at the shop, I would get an idea and just start explaining it, and I couldn't really stop. I'd just keep going and going, talking over people, barely even stopping to take a breath. I could see they were trying to get back to work or move on, but I just kept talking.
During that period when you were talking more and feeling wired, did you feel unusually happy, euphoric, or perhaps more irritable than usual?

Yeah, I definitely felt unusually happy. There were a couple of weeks where I just felt almost too good, honestly. Like I was on top of the world, like the whole city was mine. But at the same time, I was also really irritable. If one of my coworkers at the shop was moving too slow or made some little comment that annoyed me, I would just snap at them. Way harder than I normally would. So it was kind of a mix of feeling great but also getting set off really easily.
About how many days in a row did that period of feeling 'on top of the world' and having all that extra energy last?

I'm not exactly sure how many days it was in a row. Like I mentioned, it felt like a couple of weeks overall. I wasn't really keeping track on a calendar or counting the days or anything... it was just a solid stretch of time where I was going non-stop.

During these last nine months, besides feeling like a letdown and having those thoughts about not wanting to wake up, have you also been experiencing other symptoms like a significant loss of interest in activities you usually enjoy, or feeling physically slowed down or restless almost every day?

Yeah, definitely the loss of interest part. Um... lately I can just walk right past my sketchbook, or skip volleyball, and I just ignore the volunteer group texts without feeling much of anything. It's weird because those used to be the things that made me feel like myself, you know? But now I just don't have the drive for them. I haven't really noticed feeling physically slowed down or restless every day, though. Just... not caring about the stuff I used to enjoy.
